questions.q: What is the name of the glass and metal pyramid that serves as the main entrance to a world-famous museum in Paris?
questions.n: I.M. Pei designed this structure to serve as a central entrance and light well, modernizing the circulation of the historic palace.

questions.q: Which I.M. Pei project in Hong Kong is famous for its triangular glass facets and 'bamboo-like' structural expression?
questions.n: Pei used the symbolism of bamboo—representing strength and growth—to inspire the building's distinctive bracing system.

questions.q: For which presidential library did I.M. Pei use a dramatic glass-enclosed atrium overlooking the harbor in Boston?
questions.n: Pei's design utilizes a stark white concrete tower juxtaposed against a dark glass pavilion.

questions.q: What is the name of the museum in Qatar, designed by Pei in his 90s, that draws inspiration from ancient Islamic architecture?
questions.n: Pei studied Islamic history and traveled to Tunisia to find the 'essence' of the style, resulting in a geometric, stacked volume.

questions.q: I.M. Pei is often associated with which specific 'school' or variation of Modernism that emphasizes clean, sharp, geometric lines?
questions.n: Pei's work refined the principles of High Modernism through the use of sophisticated, precise Euclidean geometries.

questions.q: Who is the lead architect/firm responsible for the design of the Neo Series (formerly the Net Series) in BGC?
questions.n: In collaboration with local firm W.V. Coscolluela, Oppenheim designed these towers to be high-performance, sustainable workplaces.

questions.q: The Neo buildings are famous for being the first office towers in the Philippines to achieve what specific local green building certification?
questions.n: Net Lima (now Seven Neo) was the pilot project for the Philippine Green Building Council's BERDE rating system.

questions.q: Which specific building in the series was rebranded as Seven Neo, known for its distinctive sun-shading 'fins' and vertical gardens?
questions.n: The design features a 'diagonal' sun-shading system that drastically reduces the building's cooling load.

questions.q: What is the primary design strategy used in the Neo buildings to reduce solar heat gain while maintaining a glass-heavy aesthetic?
questions.n: The use of horizontal and vertical aluminum fins (brise-soleil) protects the facade from direct tropical solar radiation.

questions.q: In the context of BGC's development, the Neo series is often cited as a pioneer in what type of real estate development?
questions.n: The series was specifically designed to accommodate the infrastructure needs of the growing outsourcing industry in the early 2000s.

questions.q: Which of the 'Fathers' is responsible for the Bauhaus school and the Pan Am Building (MetLife) in New York?
questions.n: Gropius was the founding director of the Bauhaus and later became a professor at Harvard.

questions.q: Who is the Swiss-French architect who developed the Modulor—an anthropometric scale of proportions?
questions.n: The Modulor was based on the human body and the golden ratio, intended to improve the appearance and function of architecture.

questions.q: Which architect is known for his 'Skin and Bone' architecture and the Barcelona Pavilion?
questions.n: His buildings utilized steel frames (bone) and glass enclosures (skin) to achieve ultimate transparency and minimalism.

questions.q: Which American 'Father' rejected the European International Style in favor of Organic Architecture and the 'Prairie Style'?
questions.n: Wright believed architecture should be uniquely American and integrated with the site's natural topography.

questions.q: Which building by Le Corbusier is considered the prime example of 'Brutalist' architecture, featuring a massive concrete frame and colorful 'brise-soleil'?
questions.n: This massive residential block introduced 'beton brut' (raw concrete) as a finished material, sparking the Brutalist movement.

questions.q: What is the name of Philip Johnson's private residence in Connecticut, consisting of a simple rectangular prism with entirely glass walls?
questions.n: Built in 1949, this house was inspired by Mies van der Rohe's Farnsworth House but completed earlier.

questions.q: Philip Johnson famously curated the 1932 exhibition at MoMA that introduced what style to the American public?
questions.n: Along with Henry-Russell Hitchcock, Johnson defined the rules for a new, ornament-free global architecture.

questions.q: Which building by Johnson features a controversial 'broken-pediment' top, often compared to a Chippendale furniture piece?
questions.n: This building's use of historical ornament marked Johnson's final break from Modernism into Post-Modernism.

questions.q: In collaboration with Mies van der Rohe, Johnson worked on the interior design of which iconic New York skyscraper?
questions.n: Johnson designed the Four Seasons Restaurant and other interior spaces for Mies's bronze-clad masterpiece.

questions.q: What was the title of the 1988 MoMA exhibition Johnson curated that helped launch the careers of architects like Zaha Hadid and Frank Gehry?
o: Less is More: The Legacy of Mies
questions.n: The exhibition explored 'unstable' forms and the fragmentation of building volumes.

questions.q: Who designed the LKG Tower in Ayala Avenue, famous for its distinct 'ribbon-like' facade?
questions.n: The tower's design is notable for the sharp, angular 'ribbon' that carves through the building's facade.

questions.q: Which National Artist designed the Philippine Stock Exchange building in BGC (The 'T-shaped' tower)?
questions.n: The firm designed the unified trading floor and office tower in a bold, geometric Modernist style.

questions.q: Who is the architect of the Zuellig Building in Makati, the first building in the Philippines to receive a LEED Platinum certification?
questions.n: This collaboration resulted in a glass tower featuring an all-glass facade with low-E ceramic frit to reduce solar heat.

questions.q: Which architect designed the PBCom Tower, which held the title of the tallest building in the Philippines for many years?
questions.n: This 52-story skyscraper was the tallest from 2000 until the completion of the Grand Hyatt in 2017.

questions.q: The Pacific Star Building in Makati was designed by which notable architect?
questions.n: This building was once the tallest in the country and is known for its distinctive 29-story high-rise and adjacent low-rise crescent.
